name: Mercury Rev
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Four Buffalo film students made soundtracks for movies, got shut down by the mayor of Denver, nearly broke apart in debt, and then came out of a Catskills attic with strings, Levon Helm and NME's album of the year.

hero.by: Mercury Rev at All Tomorrow's Parties, 2004. Photo: Stinco di Porco, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Scoring films for a band that didn't exist
eras.text: In Rust Belt Buffalo, a handful of SUNY students played in a flute-and-Casio indie band called Shady Crady and studied under drone pioneer Tony Conrad. Mercury Rev started as a way to score their own student films, with Dave Fridmann recording them as coursework an hour south in Fredonia, while Jonathan Donahue was off playing guitar in The Flaming Lips.

years.h: Shady Crady opens for Sonic Youth in Buffalo
years.p: Sean "Grasshopper" Mackowiak plays bass, Suzanne Thorpe plays flute and David Baker sings over a Casio SK-1. They take the first of three local support slots when [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] come through town.

years.h: Jonathan Donahue books the Flaming Lips, then goes on the road with them
years.p: Donahue books shows for SUNY Buffalo's student union. The Flaming Lips play there opening for [[Throwing Muses|b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8]], and he drops out to work their smoke and bubble machines.
years.xp:
By 1990's In a Priest Driven Ambulance Donahue was the Lips' second guitarist. Wayne Coyne credited him with the band's home-recording turn: "He had this little cassette 4-track," Coyne told Rolling Stone.

That album was also the first to carry the credit "Produced by Dave Fridmann", a music-production student Donahue was about to bring into his own project.

years.h: Mercury Rev forms to score student films and nature documentaries
years.p: The band improvises soundtracks for films shown in local galleries, and jams along to nature shows on TV. Fridmann records them at SUNY Fredonia in off-hours, as his coursework, at bargain rates.
years.xp:
Gear was whatever was lying around: Donahue played guitar through a jury-rigged TV speaker, and songs went onto answering-machine cassettes. Fridmann added enough bass and household-appliance noises to become a member, and drummer Jimy Chambers joined late in the sessions.

Grasshopper credited [[Tony Conrad|39b56aa8-5d36-49ab-ae5e-c3aa836b6620]]'s classes, where students praised a work they hated one week and trashed one they loved the next. Chambers on his own parts: "What you hear is me not knowing what to do and being really uncomfortable."

eras.title: Too weird for Lollapalooza
eras.text: A tiny British label put out the first album and the UK weeklies did the rest: the band were booked at Reading before they'd played half a dozen shows. Columbia signed them after the Nevermind gold rush, Beggars Banquet took Boces in Britain, and the touring wore down a group that had never meant to play live.

years.h: Yerself Is Steam comes out on Mint Films in Britain
years.p: Eight songs, closing with the 12-minute 'Very Sleepy Rivers'. The title is a misheard 'your self-esteem' from the opener, 'Chasing a Bee'.
years.xp: The final mixes were settled by whoever got to the faders last, Pitchfork reports. Columbia's later CD split 'Very Sleepy Rivers' across dozens of index points, and a video for 'Chasing a Bee' was shot at the abandoned hospital on North Brother Island in the Bronx.

years.h: Melody Maker flies a writer to Fredonia before the band has played a show
years.p: Chris Roberts arrives to review a live band that doesn't exist yet, so Mercury Rev book a local bar gig for him. Baker remembers the first show as near a school, not in a club.

years.h: Donahue quits the Flaming Lips after Hit to Death in the Future Head
years.p: After creative disagreements with Wayne Coyne, Donahue leaves the Lips once the album is recorded and goes back to Buffalo full time.

years.h: Reading Festival books them for their third-ever gig
years.p: The British press buzz lands Mercury Rev on the Reading bill. Their fourth gig is opening for [[Bob Dylan|72c536dc-7137-4477-a521-567eeb840fa8]] at Yale.
years.xp: Pitchfork counts Reading as the third show; Baker told The Quietus it was the fifth. Either way it came months before Nirvana's Nevermind, with the UK weeklies selling the band as the "alternative to the alternative".

years.src: Pitchfork · The Quietus: Boces · Wikipedia: Yerself Is Steam
years.h: Rough Trade's US arm goes under and Columbia signs the band
years.p: Columbia reissues Yerself Is Steam in America with 'Car Wash Hair' added, a trumpet-lit single featuring [[Dean Wareham|a21a3ff2-064c-452d-8aea-3d4039ab70d6]] of [[Galaxie 500|4de3cfed-b459-42bd-bfbb-7a843fbc73df]].
years.xp: Baker remembered Columbia telling them they could do what they wanted. "Well, that's what we are going to do," he told The Quietus. The same year brought the Lego My Ego bonus disc of non-album tracks and John Peel sessions.

years.src: The Quietus: Boces · Wikipedia: Boces · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: Boces: Beggars Banquet in Britain, Columbia in the US
years.p: Self-produced, named after New York's BOCES vocational-school system, with flutes, harps, brass and a choir. Everyone wrote, and everyone's song got blown up by somebody else.
years.xp:
Baker described a six-way free-for-all: Chambers into '60s records, Fridmann putting on Steely Dan, Thorpe trying to beat the guitars with her flute. "They knew their song was going to get blown up," he said.

It reached No. 43 in the UK, the band's first album to chart there.

years.big: "Like a bus idling out of control"
years.h: Denver's mayor pulls the plug at Lollapalooza
years.p: On the second stage at Fiddler's Green, between a chainsaw juggler and [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]], the volume drops mid-'Very Sleepy Rivers'. Security drags the soundman off the board. That's how the mayor described them.
years.xp:
Pitchfork tells it: the mayor of Denver was walking the grounds, heard the set and demanded it be stopped. The band were taken off for being too loud and, in the official version, out of control.

Pitchfork called his line an astute piece of music criticism.

q: They asked me, but I had been wanting to leave.
years.src: The Quietus: David Baker · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: David Baker leaves after the Boces tour
years.p: Baker cites musical and personal disputes, and says it was mutual. He goes on to record as Shady and later Variety Lights.
years.xp:
Baker told The Quietus that Donahue "had a vision, and he wanted more piece of the pie," and recalled Donahue not sharing the setlist before a Royal Albert Hall show. He stayed on good terms; his 1994 Shady record used 50 musicians across several countries.

Baker wasn't the only one leaving the stage: Fridmann's production work kept him off the road, and John DeVries and then Gerald Menke covered bass live.

eras.title: Broke, unmanaged and nearly done
eras.text: With Donahue now singing, the third album veered from noise to lullaby and sold almost nothing. What followed was debt, a fight with the label, no manager, no lawyers, no drummer, and two founders who'd stopped speaking.

years.src: Wikipedia: See You on the Other Side · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: See You on the Other Side on Beggars Banquet in the UK
years.p: The first album without Baker, out in September in the US on Work. [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]] directs the video for 'Young Man's Stride', next to free-jazz blowouts and the soft 'Sudden Ray of Hope'.
play: See You on the Other Side

years.h: As Harmony Rockets, one 40-minute track
years.p: Paralyzed Mind of the Archangel Void, on Big Cat, is a single improvised psychedelic piece. They'd play it again at All Tomorrow's Parties in 2009, with Thorpe back.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deserter's Songs · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev · Far Out · The Quietus: Donahue on Deserter's Songs
years.h: Debt, a label fight, and Jimy Chambers gone
years.p: See You on the Other Side doesn't sell. The band end up in debt, in conflict with their label, and without manager, lawyers or drummer.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's Deserter's Songs article says the band asked to be released from their deal; Far Out says Beggars dropped them. Donahue later talked about two nervous breakdowns in this stretch, and he and Grasshopper were struggling with drugs and relationships.

Grasshopper went to stay at a Jesuit guest house upstate. "Everything had completely ground to a halt," Donahue told The Quietus.

years.src: The Quietus: Donahue on Deserter's Songs · Far Out · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: The Chemical Brothers call, and Donahue says yes
years.p: Donahue sings on 'The Private Psychedelic Reel', the closer of [[The Chemical Brothers|1946a82a-f927-40c2-8235-38d64f50d043]]' Dig Your Own Hole. He'd been writing simple piano melodies and listening to children's records.
years.xp: Donahue called it a sun-through-the-clouds moment: "I almost cried, because I couldn't believe someone remembered me and the band." The call pushed him to patch things up with Grasshopper.

eras.title: Strings, Levon Helm and an NME crown
eras.text: The band moved to Donahue's hometown of Kingston, New York, and rebuilt the sound from piano, strings, horns and saws. V2 signed them late in the sessions, and the record nobody was waiting for made them pop stars in Britain.

years.cap: Mercury Rev with Suzanne Thorpe, c. 1998
years.src: Wikipedia: Deserter's Songs · The Quietus: Donahue on Deserter's Songs
years.h: Two members of the Band turn up on the Catskills record
years.p: [[Levon Helm|392baa89-ea47-4de6-8dc0-fdac3ec85509]] drums on 'Opus 40' and Garth Hudson plays saxophones on 'Hudson Line'. Fridmann mixes at Tarbox Road with strings and woodwinds instead of distortion.
years.xp:
Donahue recorded much of it in his attic in the Catskill Mountains. The finished album was mastered to 35mm magnetic film.

"It had the feeling of rebirth," Donahue told The Quietus, "of going down to the grave for quite a while and lying down there in the darkness."

q: We're like the Doors biography, in reverse.
years.src: Wikipedia: Deserter's Songs · Pitchfork · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: Deserter's Songs on V2, and NME's album of the year
years.p: It reaches No. 27 in the UK and the Chemical Brothers hand out advance copies. 'Holes' later turns up in Sing 2.
years.xp:
Donahue's fuller line, as quoted by Pitchfork: all their weirdness happened first, then they got sorted out. Pitchfork also credits the album with inspiring a young Coldplay.

Wikipedia reports UK sales of 100,000 and a BPI gold certification.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deserter's Songs · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: 'Goddess on a Hiway' hits No. 26 in Britain
years.p: Their first UK Top 40 single. 'Delta Sun Bottleneck Stomp' and 'Opus 40' follow it into the Top 40 in 1999.

years.h: Suzanne Thorpe and Jimy Chambers leave after the sessions
years.p: Jeff Mercel, who'd played on the album, comes in on drums. Thorpe turns to Deep Listening and academic work; Chambers forms Odiorne.

years.h: On the road with the Flaming Lips again
years.p: Wikipedia credits the shared touring with helping launch the Lips' The Soft Bulletin, also produced by Fridmann during the same stretch.

years.cap: Mercury Rev on the Other Stage at Glastonbury
years.h: All Is Dream reaches No. 11, their best UK chart placing
years.p: [[Tony Visconti|9472e6e4-3e13-430a-900d-6f075720a5c6]] arranges strings and plays Mellotron. Fridmann now co-produces and plays bass in the studio only.

years.cap: Jonathan Donahue sings 'The Dark Is Rising' at Glastonbury, June 2002
years.h: 'The Dark Is Rising' reaches No. 16, their biggest UK single
years.p: It goes to No. 2 on the UK indie chart. Paul Dillon and Carlos Anthony Molina fill out the touring band.

eras.title: A band that got sorted out
eras.text: Mercury Rev settled into a steadier run on V2: a Top 20 record, a film score, a doubled release in 2008 and a tour playing Deserter's Songs start to finish.

years.h: The Secret Migration goes Top 20 in the UK
years.p: The fifth album reaches No. 16, and 'In a Funny Way' gets to No. 28. Carlos Anthony Molina plays keys and bass.

years.h: A film score and a best-of in the same year
years.p: Mercury Rev release the Hello Blackbird soundtrack and The Essential Mercury Rev: Stillness Breathes 1991–2006.

years.h: Snowflake Midnight, plus a free album on the side
years.p: Released alongside Strange Attractor, a free MP3 album of instrumentals. Jeff Mercel leaves afterward.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deserter's Songs · Wikipedia: Mercury Rev
years.h: Deserter's Songs comes back as a double-disc deluxe edition
years.p: Demos and remixes are added, and Mercel rejoins on tour to play the album.

eras.title: Bella Union, Bobbie Gentry and born horses
eras.text: After seven years without a studio album, the founders went on without Fridmann behind the desk for the first time. A Midlake keyboardist joined, and the band reimagined a forgotten 1968 record with a different singer on every song.

years.h: The Light in You, the first Rev album Fridmann didn't co-produce
years.p: Out on Bella Union, it reaches No. 39 in the UK. Officially the band is now a duo, with Jesse Chandler, ex-[[Midlake|da90b5da-349e-4906-a0b4-805f5e46190d]], among the regular players.

years.h: Bobbie Gentry's 1968 album, with a new voice on every track
years.p: [[Lucinda Williams|21685b15-3074-446e-aa1d-ff7157014f53]], [[Norah Jones|985c709c-7771-4de3-9024-7bda29ebe3f9]], [[Beth Orton|214d84a5-e9e5-4432-af95-8c84da7ba4c0]], [[Hope Sandoval|bc1cc75d-ab68-41b2-a135-3b62f41ea266]], [[Phoebe Bridgers|96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86]] and actress Carice van Houten are among the singers. It reaches No. 32 in the UK.
play: Bobbie Gentry's The Delta Sweete Revisited

years.h: Born Horses comes out on Bella Union
years.p: Announced in June with the single 'Patterns'. Keyboardist Marion Genser has been a member since 2021, and Joe Magistro takes the drums.
